evals.name: build-highlight-extension
evals.prompt: I want to build a Chrome extension that highlights code blocks on GitHub with a syntax-highlighting overlay. When I click the extension icon, a popup should show a toggle to enable/disable highlighting and a dropdown to pick a color theme. The content script should find all <pre><code> blocks on the page and wrap them in a highlighted container. Use Manifest V3. Keep it clean.
evals.expected_output: Three files: manifest.json, content.js, popup.html + popup.js, background.js
expectations: manifest.json uses host_permissions (not permissions) for URL pattern matching
Content script uses const/let declarations (not var)
Message listener returns true for async sendResponse calls
Leverages a real syntax highlighting library instead of a custom regex tokenizer
Handles SPA navigation (e.g., MutationObserver on title changes)
Code is organized into modular, single-responsibility functions

evals.name: fix-messaging-bug
evals.expected_output: Explanation of the bug (missing return true) and other anti-patterns found
expectations: Identifies missing return true as the root cause for async sendResponse
Identifies raw Response object issue (fetch returns Response, needs .json())
Identifies missing error handling (no .catch() on fetch promise)
Recommends chrome.runtime.lastError check in popup callback
Provides fixed code examples for both background.js and popup.js

evals.name: audit-extension-code
evals.expected_output: Structured findings report with severity ratings and fix recommendations
expectations: Identifies that host permissions pattern (*://*/*) is in permissions instead of host_permissions
Identifies var declarations polluting global scope in content script
Identifies lack of input validation in background message handler
Identifies setInterval in service worker (should use chrome.alarms for persistence)
Identifies missing version field in manifest.json
Identifies sendResponse called without return true
Identifies doit() function defined but never invoked
